claim: Saucier v. Katz, 533 U.S. 194 (2001), decided June 18, 2001, held that the qualified immunity inquiry is "not susceptible of fusion with the question whether unreasonable force was used in making the arrest" and mandated a rigid two-step sequence.
evidence: A qualified immunity ruling requires an analysis not susceptible of fusion with the question whether unreasonable force was used in making the arrest. ... The initial inquiry is whether a constitutional right would have been violated on the facts alleged, for if no right would have been violated, there is no need for further inquiry into immunity.
